note: One people, tradition or figure from history for every European country. A tradition with a name and a place, never 'a Frenchman in a beret'.

ALB.name: Iso-polyphony singer
ALB.note: Four voices, one of them holding a single note underneath.

ALD.name: Åland windjammer sailor
ALD.note: The last great sailing ships in the world worked from here.

AND.name: Pyrenean shepherd
AND.note: Up the mountain in summer, down again before the snow.

AUT.name: Alpine cowherd
AUT.note: In autumn the cows come down wearing flowers and enormous bells.

BEL.name: Gille of Binche
BEL.note: Wax masks, ostrich feathers, and oranges thrown to the crowd.

BGR.name: Kukeri
BGR.note: Hairy monsters hung with cowbells, chasing winter away.

BIH.name: Sevdah singer
BIH.note: Slow songs of longing, sung in a room too small for them.

BLR.name: Kalyady mummer
BLR.note: A goat, a star and a song, going house to house in midwinter.

CHE.name: Alphorn player
CHE.note: A horn as long as three people, once used to call across valleys.

CZE.name: Bohemian glassblower
CZE.note: Glass gathered on a pipe, and blown while it is still glowing.

DEU.name: Sorbs
DEU.note: A Slavic people in eastern Germany, with painted eggs and their own language.

EST.name: Kihnu islander
EST.note: On this island the women kept the old songs, and the motorbikes.

FRA.name: Breton
FRA.note: A Celtic corner of France, with bagpipes and a language of its own.

FRO.name: Faroese chain dancer
FRO.note: Everyone holds hands in a ring and sings the story as they step.

GBR.name: Highland piper
GBR.note: Bagpipes that can be heard from the far side of a glen.

GGY.name: Guernsey knitter
GGY.note: The fisherman's jumper is named after this island.

HRV.name: Klapa singer
HRV.note: Men in a stone alley, singing with no instruments at all.

HUN.name: Csikós
HUN.note: Horsemen of the puszta, who ride standing on two horses at once.

IMN.name: Manx Gaelic singer
IMN.note: A language that nearly disappeared, and is being sung back.

IRL.name: Irish dancer
IRL.note: Feet like lightning, arms perfectly still.

JEY.name: Jersey oysterman
JEY.note: The tide goes out so far here that the island nearly doubles.

KOS.name: Rugova highlander
KOS.note: Stone villages up a gorge, and a dance with swords.

LIE.name: Alpine cowherd
LIE.note: In autumn the cows come down wearing flowers and enormous bells.

LTU.name: Cross crafter
LTU.note: Carved wooden crosses, and a hill with a hundred thousand of them.

LUX.name: Echternach dancing procession
LUX.note: A procession that hops its way through the town every spring.

LVA.name: Suiti
LVA.note: A small community whose women improvise songs on the spot.

MCO.name: Grimaldi knight
MCO.note: In 1297 a man disguised as a monk took the rock — and never gave it back.

MDA.name: Lăutar
MDA.note: Wedding fiddlers who can play for two days without a sheet of music.

MKD.name: Galičnik wedding
MKD.note: Once a year, one wedding for the whole empty mountain village.

MLT.name: Luzzu fisherman
MLT.note: Boats painted with an eye on the bow, to watch the sea for you.

MNE.name: Njeguši highlander
MNE.note: A village on the black mountain that gave the country its name.

NLD.name: Frisians
NLD.note: Their own language, and a skating race past eleven towns in one day.

POL.name: Górale
POL.note: Highlanders of the Tatras, in felt hats and wooden houses.

PRT.name: Fado singer
PRT.note: Songs about missing something you cannot quite name.

ROU.name: Maramureș woodcarver
ROU.note: Gates and churches carved from oak, with spires like needles.

SMR.name: Crossbowman of San Marino
SMR.note: A shooting contest under the towers, in medieval dress, every year.

SRB.name: Gusle player
SRB.note: One string, a horsehair bow, and a poem that lasts all evening.

SVK.name: Fujara player
SVK.note: A shepherd's flute taller than the shepherd.

SVN.name: Kurent
SVN.note: A shaggy sheepskin monster with a long red tongue, ringing bells at winter.

UKR.name: Zaporozhian Cossack
UKR.note: A free camp of riders on an island in the Dnipro.

VAT.name: Swiss Guard
VAT.note: Striped uniforms and a halberd, guarding the smallest country there is.
